summary: This is a small Java class that models a single cookie. Each Cookie object stores one flavor, set when the object is created, and can describe itself as a sentence.

lines.text: Declares the class, which acts as the blueprint every cookie object is built from. The name is capitalised by Java convention and must match the file name Cookie.java.
The one piece of data each cookie carries. `private` keeps it hidden from outside code so nothing can tamper with it, and `final` means once a cookie has a flavor it can never be changed.
The constructor: special code that runs when someone writes `new Cookie(...)`. It demands a flavor, so it is impossible to create a cookie without one.

Copies the value passed in to the object's own field. `this.flavor` is the field belonging to this object, while plain `flavor` is the parameter, which is how Java tells the two apart when they share a name.
A method that reports on the object rather than changing it. It returns a String instead of printing, so the caller decides what to do with the text.
Builds the sentence by joining text with the stored flavor using the `+` operator. The method can read `flavor` directly because it lives inside the same class.
